paper_metadata.title: Quantum Algorithm for Local-Volatility Option Pricing via the Kolmogorov Equation

experiments.description: End-to-end quantum simulation of the forward Kolmogorov PDE for a single-asset local-volatility European vanilla option, using Schrödingerisation, block-encoding/Hamiltonian simulation, and swap-test-based payoff recovery.

algorithm.variant: Schrödingerisation-based Hamiltonian simulation of the forward Kolmogorov equation with time-dependent local volatility and swap-test retrieval

hyperparameters.volatility_form: sigma(s, tau) = sum_{k=0..Ds} sum_{q=0..Dt} C_kq s^k tau^q
hyperparameters.low_rank_separable_approximation: sigma_lr(s, tau) = sum_{m=1..R} alpha_m r_m(s) q_m(tau)
hyperparameters.rank_R_assumption: R = O(1) or at most O(polylog(1/epsilon))
hyperparameters.block_encoding_log_factor: c = O(log n + log ny + log nw)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The asset-price distribution p(x,t) is encoded into amplitudes of an n-qubit register; the initial condition p(s,0)=delta(s-S0) is represented by the computational basis state |S0> or a sharply peaked Gaussian approximation. Auxiliary registers encode the Schrödingerisation qumode and clock dimension.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute the discounted option price V0 = e^{-int_0^T r(s) ds} E[C0(S_T) | S_0] by evolving the forward Kolmogorov PDE for p(s,t) and then evaluating the expected payoff via overlap with a payoff state.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on positive momentum eigenvectors of the auxiliary qumode; periodic boundary conditions assumed on a sufficiently wide domain.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Pseudo-Hamiltonian H_LV from the forward PDE, embedded into a unitary Hamiltonian H = I ⊗ I_w ⊗ p_y + H_LVS(tau = x_y).

problem_instance.description: European vanilla call/put pricing under a local-volatility model; single-asset forward Kolmogorov PDE, with Black-Scholes used as an illustrative special case for overlap analysis and closed-form density.

dataset_specification.description: No market dataset is used in the reported experiment; the paper uses model-based inputs (spot S0, strike K, maturity T, rates, and a polynomial/separable local-volatility surface).

cnot_count.initial_state_preparation_basis_state: at most n X gates for |S0>
cnot_count.auxiliary_state_preparation: O(nw log nw) for smooth cut-off / piecewise polynomial preparation

quantum_resources.num_shots: O(1/epsilon_V0^2) via swap test; more specifically O(1/epsilon_st^2 log(1/delta)) copies for overlap estimation

implementation_details.classical_solver: Finite-difference time stepping and matrix-exponential action are discussed as classical baselines in Appendix B
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize the spatial domain; encode the initial delta-like condition; approximate the local-volatility surface by a polynomial or low-rank separable expansion; prepare payoff state via piecewise-polynomial state preparation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use a swap test to estimate overlaps |<C0|p(T)>|^2 and |<+^n|p(T)>|^2, then reconstruct the option price from the closed-form scaling relations; shot-noise and discretization errors are O(Nshots^{-1/2}) and O(2^{-n}), respectively.

results.value: at most n X gates for |S0>

results.unit: gate complexity for auxiliary state preparation

results.value: c = O(log n + log ny + log nw)

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic in number of grid points
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical finite-difference time stepping / matrix-exponential action
speedup_claims.conditions: single-asset PDE discretized on N = 2^n grid points; asymptotic comparison in Appendix B
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes the dominant momentum-term norm scales as 2^(2n), limiting the achievable speedup to polynomial rather than exponential for the single-asset case.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical methods suffering from curse of dimensionality
speedup_claims.conditions: multi-asset basket options / d-dimensional forward Kolmogorov PDEs
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is asymptotic; no numerical benchmark is reported. The paper states linear scaling in d for initial-state preparation and polynomial evolution cost in d.

speedup_claims.conditions: simplified scaling expressions for the single-asset forward PDE
speedup_claims.caveats: Presented as a simplified asymptotic comparison, not an empirical benchmark.

experiments.description: Forward-vs-backward overlap analysis in the Black-Scholes special case, used to justify choosing the forward Kolmogorov formulation for quantum simulation.

algorithm.variant: State-overlap comparison between forward and backward PDE solutions in the Black-Scholes model

hyperparameters.discount_factor: ignored in the overlap plot analysis
hyperparameters.state_encoding: normalized quantum states for p(s,t) and C(s,t)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: The forward solution p(s,T) and backward solution C(s,T) are each normalized and encoded as quantum states; overlaps with the initial states are computed.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compare |<p(0)|p(T)>| and |<C(0)|C(T)>| to assess which PDE formulation is more suitable for quantum simulation.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: None beyond normalization and the assumed discretization of the state space.

problem_instance.description: Black-Scholes single-asset option-pricing dynamics used as a diagnostic example for overlap decay.

dataset_specification.description: Analytical Black-Scholes density and backward solution are used; no external dataset.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute analytical Black-Scholes forward density and backward solution; normalize both states.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Plot and compare overlaps; the paper reports forward overlap decays rapidly while backward overlap remains above about 0.995 for relevant maturities.

results.value: exponentially decaying overlap for forward state

speedup_claims.factor: forward formulation is more suitable for quantum simulation than backward formulation
speedup_claims.conditions: Black-Scholes single-asset diagnostic example; based on overlap decay of normalized states
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a suitability argument rather than a runtime speedup. The backward state remains very close to the initial state, making it hard to resolve on a quantum computer.

experiments.description: Scalability analysis for a multi-asset forward Kolmogorov local-volatility model, showing polynomial dependence on dimension and linear initial-state preparation in d.

algorithm.variant: Multi-asset forward Kolmogorov PDE simulation with Schrödingerisation and block-encoding

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each asset is discretized on an n-qubit register; the full state space has dimension 2^(dn). The initial condition is a product of delta states |S_{1,0}> ⊗ ... ⊗ |S_{d,0}>.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve the d-asset forward Kolmogorov PDE and compute the expected payoff of a multi-asset European claim.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Not specified beyond the same discretization and boundary assumptions as the single-asset case.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Multi-asset forward Kolmogorov operator with drift, diffusion, and cross-derivative terms.

problem_instance.description: General d-asset local-volatility pricing problem; representative multi-asset payoffs include arithmetic basket, spread/exchange, geometric basket, and digital options.

dataset_specification.description: No empirical dataset; the paper provides generic multi-asset payoff forms and asymptotic scaling only.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare each asset’s initial basis state independently; construct multi-asset payoff states as factorized or low-rank linear combinations of factorized terms.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: No numerical benchmark run is reported; the paper states asymptotic scaling only.

results.value: linear in d for block-encoding query cost

speedup_claims.factor: exponential speedup with respect to dimension
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical multi-asset PDE solvers suffering from curse of dimensionality
speedup_claims.conditions: high-dimensional basket options / d-asset forward Kolmogorov PDEs
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper’s explicit theorem states polynomial dependence in d for the quantum method and linear initial-state preparation in d; the exponential advantage is relative to classical scaling in the full state-space dimension 2^(dn), not a measured benchmark.

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming second-order derivative order, Theta(d^2) operator norm, Theta(d^2 s^2) sparsity, and linear-in-d block-encoding cost
speedup_claims.caveats: Asymptotic derivation only; no numerical experiments reported.
